title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after a traffic stop on July 23. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, and her 12-year-old sister were pulled over on Calle Duran because a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, confusing a final 2 for a 7 and flagging the car as stolen in Rio Rancho. Officers handcuffed both sisters and placed them in separate police vehicles before realizing the mistake. Jaclynn had asked police to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the younger girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child.

The lawsuits, filed January 3 in state District Court, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restricted movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when he was wrongly stopped in April after being mistaken for an armed robbery suspect and forced to kneel with his hands on his head. The city of Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. No next court date or city response is mentioned.
